plan_shape: equal 15B from each of four formats (faq, math, table, tutorial)
status: MEASURED. All four configs counted under allenai/dolma2-tokenizer via exact nested-leaf parquet footers plus 160 random row groups (160,000 rewrites tokenized). Phase 0's 0.00B and its card-only figures are superseded.
schema_note: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT QUERY, NOT ASSUMED. The rewrite is at `rollout_results[0].text`. Full shape: FinePhrase carries 12 columns = the 11 columns of its FineWeb-Edu parent plus `rollout_results`. `rollout_results` is a LIST of STRUCT{finish_reason: string, text: string, usage: STRUCT{completion_tokens: int64, prompt_tokens: int64, prompt_tokens_details: null, total_tokens: int64}} -- verified against /info `dataset_info.features` for configs math, table and tutorial (all three byte-identical schemas) and against /first-rows for faq and all. Exactly ONE rollout per document, always: /statistics reports column `rollout_results` with column_type=list and mean=median=min=max=1.0 over 842,000 rows, and all 34 faq rows sampled had len(rollout_results)==1. So element [0] is the entire payload and there is no multi-rollout aggregation to perform. THE TRAP IS REAL AND CONFIRMED: the top-level `text` column holds the ORIGINAL, UNREPHRASED FineWeb-Edu document -- its sibling `dataset` field reads the literal string 'HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu' in 34/34 rows sampled, and `token_count` is FineWeb-Edu's own count of `text` (measured dolma2/token_count ratio 1.0091 on the original, i.e. token_count describes the ORIGINAL, never the rewrite). Counting `text` would build a corpus of unrephrased real web data labelled synthetic, at 27x the true token volume, and neither a size check nor a hash check can detect it because both the bytes and the digest would be internally consistent.
schema_note_phase0c_addendum: Phase 0's schema claims are all CONFIRMED at n=160,000 (rollouts_per_row min=max=1 in every one of 160 row groups across all four configs; PRESERVED VERBATIM above). ONE FIGURE IN IT IS NOW CORRECTED: the trap's magnitude is 2.9x, not 27x. Phase 0's 27x came from dividing the original document's ~1,100 tokens by the head sample's anomalous 40.5 tokens/rewrite. Measured properly, per config the overcount from reading `text` instead of `rollout_results[0].text` is faq 2.25x, tutorial 2.37x, math 3.80x, table 3.92x, whole corpus 2.90x (478.15B rewrite vs 1,386.8B original). The trap is NO LESS SEVERE -- it substitutes 1.39 TRILLION tokens of unrephrased real FineWeb-Edu for the synthetic pool, and because `all` repeats the same 339M source documents 4x, the substituted originals would be 4 EXACT DUPLICATES of each other, which is worse than a mere volume error. Only the multiplier changes.

measurement_method.headline: EXACT nested-leaf parquet footers + calibration + sampled tokens/byte. No ratio correction was needed, because pyarrow exposes the nested leaf as its own column chunk.
measurement_method.the_nested_column_problem_and_how_it_was: The brief offered two routes: (a) read footers at LEAF level if pyarrow exposes per-leaf column chunks for the nested path, giving the exact figure; or (b) sample the ratio len(rollout_results[0].text)/parent-column-bytes and correct. WE TOOK ROUTE (a) -- IT WORKS. pyarrow 24.0.0's `ParquetFile.metadata.row_group(i).column(j).path_in_schema` returns dotted leaf paths, and FinePhrase's footers carry SIX separate leaves under rollout_results. Measured on faq/000_00000_0.parquet row group 0: `rollout_results.list.element.finish_reason` 78 B, `rollout_results.list.element.text` 1,769,213 B, `...usage.completion_tokens` 5,688 B, `...usage.prompt_tokens` 7,280 B, `...usage.prompt_tokens_details` 47 B, `...usage.total_tokens` 7,520 B. We select the ONE leaf `rollout_results.list.element.text` by exact path, so the sibling fields are never summed and route (b)'s sampling uncertainty is avoided entirely. NOTE the schema hazard route (a) also dodges: `md.schema.names` returns a FLAT 17-name list containing 'text' TWICE (index 0 = the original, index 12 = the rewrite leaf), so `.names.index('text')` -- which is exactly what the existing `_footer_chars.py` does -- silently returns the ORIGINAL. The trap is reachable through the footer path too, and matching on path_in_schema rather than index is what closes it.
measurement_method.naive_parent_overcount_quantified: Had we summed the whole `rollout_results` subtree instead of the one leaf, we would have overcounted by faq +1.02%, tutorial +1.04%, table +1.53%, math +1.68%. Small, but measured rather than assumed, and it is a systematic bias in one direction.
two_remaining_corrections_and_their_vali: PLAIN BYTE_ARRAY length prefix: parquet stores 4 bytes of length per value, and total_uncompressed_size is post-encoding. Subtracted as 4 x num_values (0.19-0.33% of the leaf here).

Nested-leaf repetition/definition levels: a nested leaf's pages also carry rep/def levels, which total_uncompressed_size includes. Rather than assume these are negligible we CALIBRATED: for every row group actually read, we compared sum(len(text.encode('utf8'))) against that same row group's footer figure minus the length prefix. Residual overhead measured at faq +0.0507%, tutorial +0.0516%, table +0.0934%, math +0.1123% -- i.e. the footer route is accurate to about one part in a thousand, and that residual is divided out of the final byte total. This is 'recompute, never trust' applied to our own estimator: the byte total is anchored on real decoded UTF-8 bytes, not on a claim about parquet internals.
measurement_method.extrapolation_from_files_to_config: Every config has ~6.8k parquet files and a footer read costs ~680 KB, so scanning all 27,104 would move ~18 GB. Instead: 250 random files per config (1,000 total), then scale by the EXACT total parquet bytes per config from the Hub tree API. The scaled quantity is leaf_bytes/parquet_file_bytes, whose across-file CV is only 0.010-0.017 -- so the extrapolation contributes well under 0.1% at n=250.
measurement_method.extrapolation_validated_against_a_known_: The same byte-ratio scaling also predicts each config's ROW COUNT, and the row counts are independently known exactly from /size. Predicted vs known: faq 339,025,809 vs 339,039,447 (-0.004%), math 338,841,497 vs 338,747,732 (+0.028%), table 338,434,368 vs 338,546,433 (-0.033%), tutorial 337,943,860 vs 337,711,099 (+0.069%). Four independent hits inside 0.07% is direct evidence the extrapolation is sound, not just internally consistent. It also RETROACTIVELY CONFIRMS Phase 0's faq row count, which had to be derived by subtraction because /size, /rows and /info all 500 for that config.
measurement_method.tokens_per_byte_sampling: 12 random row groups per config from 12 distinct random files (one random row group each), read with pf.read_row_group(n, columns=['rollout_results', 'text', 'token_count']) -- ~12,000 rewrites per config. tokens/byte is computed pooled (sum tokens / sum bytes), and its per-document CV is reported.
measurement_method.final_estimator: tokens = [ (leaf footer bytes, scaled to config) - 4 x n_values ] / (1 + calibrated_overhead) x (sampled dolma2 tokens/byte)
measurement_method.independent_cross_check: num_rows(exact, /size) x mean dolma2 tokens/doc(sampled). This shares the tokenizer but NOT the byte-total machinery, so its agreement tests the footer arithmetic. Divergence: faq 0.19%, math 0.45%, tutorial 1.46%, table 3.14%.
measurement_method.third_cross_check: The generator's own SmolLM2 completion_tokens were read from the same rows: dolma2/completion_token = faq 1.00248, tutorial 1.00049, table 0.97156, math 0.96500. dolma2 and SmolLM2 count this text within 3.5% of each other, so the card's completion-token figures are already near-dolma2 and needed little re-scaling -- which is why our measurements land so close to them.
measurement_method.datasets_server_avoided_entirely: ZERO datasets-server calls in Phase 0c. Phase 0 died on the per-IP 429 quota, and for config faq /size, /rows and /info all return HTTP 500 anyway. Everything here goes to the Hub tree API (file listing) plus HTTP Range reads against resolve/main URLs. Total traffic: ~1.1 GB of footers + ~350 MB of row groups against a 3.79 TB corpus (0.04%). All four configs are now measurable, INCLUDING faq -- Phase 0's 'needs a streaming count on Batch' is resolved without one.
measurement_method.no_dataset_download: Honored (§5.7). No load_dataset(), no hf_hub_download, no full file ever fetched. Footers via 2 Range requests per file; row groups via Range reads of individual column chunks. Nothing written to disk beyond ~30 KB of JSON (disk at 93%).
measurement_method.seeds: footer/tokenization run seed=7; cluster-variance run seed=99 (a disjoint file sample, so the short-rewrite numbers are not the same rows as the tokens/byte numbers)

sources.estimator: footer-leaf-exact (nested leaf rollout_results.list.element.text) x sampled tokens/byte
sources.confidence_note: Cross-checked by rows x mean-tokens to 0.19% and by the card to +0.30%. Extrapolation CV 0.0104 at n=250 files; footer calibration residual 0.051%; tokens/byte per-doc CV 0.148.
sources.rows_provenance: /size-derived (Phase 0, by subtraction); INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED to -0.004% by this run's byte-ratio extrapolation (339,025,809)
sources.note: Phase 0 called this 'the one config datasets-server cannot count at all'. Footers count it fine -- datasets-server was never required. Largest of the four and the second-longest rewrites.

sources.confidence_note: Cross-checked by rows x mean-tokens to 1.46% and by the card to +0.35%. Extrapolation CV 0.0105; calibration residual 0.052%; tokens/byte per-doc CV 0.148.
sources.note: Longest rewrites of the four (444 tok/doc). Phase 0's Arrow-byte cross-check predicted 146.3B; measured 147.9B -- Phase 0's cheap arithmetic was right to 1.1%.

sources.confidence_note: Cross-checked by rows x mean-tokens to 0.45% and by the card to -3.72%. The card gap is REAL and explained: dolma2 counts this text at 0.965 tokens per SmolLM2 completion token (math notation tokenizes differently), so the card's generator-side figure overstates the dolma2 count. Extrapolation CV 0.0120; calibration residual 0.112%.
sources.note: Highest tokens/byte of the four (0.2336) and the shortest-rewrite-heaviest: 12.6% under 50 tokens, 3-4x the other configs. Phase 0's Arrow arithmetic predicted 89.6B; measured 94.7B (5.4% low).

sources.confidence_note: Cross-checked by rows x mean-tokens to 3.14% (the widest of the four -- table rewrites are the most length-dispersed, CV 0.95) and by the card to -5.90%, again explained by dolma2/SmolLM2 = 0.972. Extrapolation CV 0.0168 (also the widest); calibration residual 0.093%.
sources.note: SMALLEST of the four at 86.95B, and the one config that came in below its card figure by more than 5%. Still 4.8x the 18B floor. Lowest tokens/byte (0.2010) and highest tokens/byte dispersion (CV 0.25) -- markdown table pipes and dashes tokenize unlike prose.

rewrite_to_original_ratio.method: PAIRED -- both columns read from the SAME 4,000 rows per config (16,000 pairs total), so the ratio is not two independent samples divided.
rewrite_to_original_ratio.verdict: REPHRASING COMPRESSES, HARD. Every format's rewrite is SHORTER than its source: the whole corpus is 478.15B rewrite tokens from 1,386.8B original tokens, a ratio of 0.345 -- rephrasing throws away roughly two thirds of the text. faq and tutorial retain ~43%, math and table only ~26%.
rewrite_to_original_ratio.why_the_mean_and_median_ratios_differ_so: The median PER-DOCUMENT ratio (0.31-0.71) is well above the pooled byte ratio (0.24-0.44) for every config. That is the max_tokens=2048 ceiling biting: long source documents get truncated hard while short ones are rephrased near-1:1, so the pooled ratio is dragged down by the long tail. Consequence for us: FinePhrase is NOT a uniform re-expression of FineWeb-Edu -- it systematically under-represents long documents. If document length correlates with anything we care about (and for educational text it does), the synthetic pool is length-biased relative to its own parent.
rewrite_to_original_ratio.sanity_check_on_the_original_column: dolma2 tokens / FineWeb-Edu's own `token_count` on the ORIGINAL = 0.9897-0.99905 across configs, i.e. within 1% of unity. So FineWeb-Edu's advertised counts are already dolma2-comparable, and the original column reads as the genuine parent document -- corroborating the trap diagnosis from a second direction.

short_rewrite_stats.n_note: 40 row groups per config x 4 configs x ~1000 rows = 159,961 rewrites, each row group drawn from a DIFFERENT randomly chosen parquet file (160 distinct files out of 27,104), at a random row-group offset within it. Seed 99, disjoint from the seed-7 sample used for tokens/byte.
short_rewrite_stats.sampling_method: random file x random row group, via pf.read_row_group(n, columns=['rollout_results']). NOT /first-rows.
short_rewrite_stats.verdict_on_phase0_head_sample: PHASE 0's n=34 HEAD SAMPLE WAS WRONG BY 10x, AND ITS OWN CAVEAT WAS CORRECT TO SUSPECT IT. Head sample: mean 40.5 tokens, median 33, 67.6% under 50. Properly sampled faq: mean 438.5, median 412, 5.3% under 50. Phase 0 flagged the ~437-vs-41 gap against the card and its own byte arithmetic and said 'the head is anomalously degenerate -- re-sample at random offsets before choosing a threshold'. That was the right call: the first ~34 rows of faq are a genuinely degenerate contiguous block, and parquet row order is content-clustered so a head read lands entirely inside it. The card and the byte arithmetic were right; the head sample was not.

cluster_aware_uncertainty.why_this_is_reported: A row group is 1000 CONSECUTIVE rows and FinePhrase inherits FineWeb-Edu's content-clustered row order, so 40,000 rewrites from 40 row groups are NOT 40,000 independent draws. Treating them as independent is precisely the error that made the Phase 0 head sample look precise. So the SE is computed from the SD of the 40 per-row-group statistics divided by sqrt(40), and compared against the naive binomial SE.
cluster_aware_uncertainty.interpretation: The design effect is only 1.0-1.3x, so clustering is mild at THIS scale and the intervals are genuinely tight: frac-under-50 is pinned to within +/-0.2pp and mean tokens/doc to within +/-3 tokens. Critically, the per-group RANGE is narrow too -- no row group among 160 came anywhere near the head sample's 40.5 mean or 67.6% short rate. The head block is an outlier at the very start of the split, not a recurring regime. NOTE the asymmetry this implies: 40 well-spread clusters give a tight answer, but 1 cluster (which is what a /first-rows call is) gives an arbitrarily wrong one. The lesson is spread, not volume.

degenerate_strings_verbatim.note: Distinct rewrites of <=5 dolma2 tokens, with occurrence counts, across the 160k sample. Phase 0's three examples ('No answer', 'Document:', 'A:') are the same failure family, and 'Document:' recurs in both faq (6x) and tutorial (3x) -- so it is a real prompt-echo mode, not a one-off.

short_rewrite_stats.finish_reason_significance: PHASE 0's CONCLUSION STANDS, with the mechanism now visible. `length` DOES occur (0.65-1.24% of rows -- Phase 0's 34/34 'stop' was just too small to see it), but it marks rewrites that hit max_tokens=2048, i.e. the LONGEST outputs, not the degenerate ones. Every degenerate string above carries finish_reason='stop'. So finish_reason is not merely useless as a quality filter, it is ANTI-correlated with quality: filtering on finish_reason != 'stop' would delete the 2048-token outputs and keep 'No answer'. Length remains the only signal.
short_rewrite_stats.quality_filtering_verdict: STILL WORTH DOING, BUT IT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR POOL SIZING -- and this REVERSES Phase 0's 'LOAD-BEARING AND MANDATORY' on the sizing question while keeping it on the hygiene question. A >=50-token minimum on rollout_results[0].text costs 0.2-1.3% of tokens and removes 3.4-12.6% of documents; that is cheap hygiene we should absolutely apply, and a blocklist for the recurring prompt-echo strings ('Document:', 'Answer:', 'Problem:', 'FAQ', '---', '<no text provided>', 'No table is provided.') on top. But it does NOT threaten the 15B-per-format plan: even math, the worst case, retains 98.7% of its tokens. Phase 0's fear that filtering might eat the pool was an artifact of the 68%-under-50 head sample. Do NOT set the threshold above ~200 tokens: at >=200 table loses 23% of its tokens, because table rewrites are legitimately short (a markdown table IS a short document) -- a high threshold would silently reshape the format mix rather than remove failures.

all_config_verdict.question: Is `all` a union of 4 independent corpora or 4 correlated views of the same documents?
all_config_verdict.answer: FOUR CORRELATED VIEWS OF THE SAME DOCUMENTS. Confirmed from the repo's own config declaration, not inferred. RE-VERIFIED in Phase 0c against the live cardData.
evidence: cardData declares config `all` as data_files path = ['faq/**/*.parquet','math/**/*.parquet','table/**/*.parquet','tutorial/**/*.parquet'] -- literally the concatenation of the other four configs. It is a SUPERSET by construction, and adds no data of its own. (Re-fetched 2026-07-31: unchanged.)

Card: 'Source documents in input split: 339,347,842'; 'Output samples across all configs: 1,354,044,711'. 4 x 339,347,842 = 1,357,391,368, and 1,354,044,711 / 1,357,391,368 = 99.75% -- i.e. essentially every source document was rephrased once per format, with a 0.25% generation-failure shortfall.
Per-config row counts are near-identical (338.7M / 338.5M / 337.7M / 339.0M), as expected if each is one pass over the same parent set.
Source is FineWeb-Edu config sample-350BT, a single fixed sample -- the same 339M documents feed all four prompt families.

PHASE 0c ADDITION, from the paired reads: the ORIGINAL `text` column's mean dolma2 tokens/doc is 985.5 / 1063.6 / 1008.3 / 1038.8 for faq / math / table / tutorial -- the same distribution four times over, within 8%, exactly as a shared parent set predicts. And its tokens/byte is 0.2140 / 0.2147 / 0.2151 / 0.2177, agreeing to 0.2%. Four independent 4,000-row samples of the parent look identical because they ARE the same parent.
PHASE 0c ADDITION: the file COUNT per config is 6791 / 6787 / 6772 / 6754 = 27,104 total, matching the brief's figure, and the four are within 0.5% of each other -- one pass per format.
all_config_verdict.consequence: The advertised 486.4B (measured 478.2B) is NOT 478.2B of independent tokens. It is ~339M source documents seen 4 times through 4 different prompts. Drawing 15B from each of the four formats means the SAME underlying documents appear up to 4 times in our mix, in 4 different surface forms. That is near-duplicate content that no digest-level dedup will catch, because the surface strings genuinely differ. Do NOT treat the four formats as independent sources when computing effective source diversity, and do not use `all` -- draw from the four named configs so the composition is explicit.
all_config_verdict.phase0c_quantification_of_the_hazard: Now sizable. 15B/format needs 10.1% (faq), 10.0% (tutorial), 15.8% (math), 16.7% (table) of each config's documents. If those four draws were INDEPENDENT random samples of the shared 339M parent, the expected number of source documents appearing in 2+ formats is large but the expected 4x-repeat rate is only ~0.03% of the parent -- so at 15B/format the cross-format duplication is real but modest, PROVIDED the four draws are independent. THE MITIGATION IS THEREFORE FREE AND MUST BE TAKEN: partition the parent document `id` space into four disjoint slices by hash and give each format its own slice. Then cross-format repetition is exactly ZERO by construction, at no cost in available tokens (each format needs only ~17% of its rows and a hash-quarter gives it 25%). Drawing all four from the same file ranges -- the obvious implementation -- would instead maximize the overlap. The per-row `id` column is present in every config and is FineWeb-Edu's own document id, so it is the natural join key.

category_total_note: 478.15B measured vs 486.3B card, -1.68%. The two configs that came in low (math -3.7%, table -5.9%) are explained by dolma2 counting math/table text at 0.965-0.972 tokens per SmolLM2 completion token; faq and tutorial, where the tokenizers agree to 0.25%, land within 0.35% of their card figures. The card is honest; it is just counted with a different tokenizer, which is exactly the §3.1 problem this task exists to fix. NOTE this is NOT 478.15B of independent tokens -- see all_config_verdict.
meets_3x_peak_demand_note: Peak plausible demand 6B (30% of a 20B run); 3x floor = 18B. The smallest config, table, measures 86.95B -- 4.8x the floor on its own. The category total is 26.6x the floor. Verdict is not close.
fifteen_B_per_format_note: YES for all four, MEASURED not inferred, with 5.8x-9.9x headroom each (faq 148.5B, tutorial 147.9B, math 94.7B, table 87.0B). In documents: 15B needs 34.3M (faq, 10.1% of config), 33.8M (tutorial, 10.0%), 53.4M (math, 15.8%), 56.6M (table, 16.7%). Phase 0's open worry -- that if the true mean were the head sample's 41 tokens/doc then 15B would need MORE documents than a config contains -- is now closed: the real means are 265-444 tokens/doc, so every format needs only a sixth of its rows or less. Quality filtering at >=50 tokens costs at most 1.3% of tokens and does not change this. The binding constraint on this category is NOT availability, it is the cross-format duplication in all_config_verdict.
overlaps: CRITICAL, FLAGGED PER THE BRIEF: FinePhrase is a rephrasing of HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu (config sample-350BT, split train) -- stated on the card and confirmed by the per-row `dataset` field reading 'HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu'. It therefore OVERLAPS every FineWeb-lineage real-token source in the reservoir at the DOCUMENT level: FineWeb-Edu itself, FineWeb-Edu-score-2, FineWeb, and (per README.md item 2's lineage chain) Zyda-2 and anything else containing FineWeb-Edu-score-2. Do not sum synthetic FinePhrase tokens against FineWeb-lineage real tokens as if they were disjoint pools.

PHASE 0c QUANTIFIES IT: §3.2 sources edu-web from fineweb-edu AND finepdfs-edu. The fineweb-edu half is a DIRECT document-level collision with 100% of our synthetic pool -- every synthetic document we draw has its unrephrased original eligible for the edu-web pool. FineWeb-Edu sample-350BT is ~350B tokens and its documents' dolma2 mean is ~1,010 tokens/doc over the same 339M ids, so the two pools are drawn from ONE 339M-document universe. The finepdfs-edu half is a different corpus and does not collide this way. MITIGATION, and it composes with the cross-format slicing above: exclude from the edu-web draw any FineWeb-Edu `id` that entered the synthetic draw. Same join key, one pass.

The overlap is not merely lineage bookkeeping: every FinePhrase document's ORIGINAL text is physically present in the corpus as the `text` column. If any part of the pipeline ever reads the wrong column, we ingest FineWeb-Edu twice -- once as real, once as 'synthetic'. Phase 0c adds that the footer path is ALSO vulnerable, because `md.schema.names` contains 'text' twice and `.index('text')` returns the original; only path_in_schema matching is safe.

Rephrasing defeats n-gram decontamination (see project memory: rephrased synthetic hides contamination). FineWeb-Edu does zero decontam and this pipeline has none either, so FinePhrase inherits and then CONCEALS whatever eval contamination FineWeb-Edu carries. Phase 0c adds a mechanism note: the measured rewrite/original token ratio is 0.345, i.e. rephrasing is aggressive rewriting rather than light paraphrase, which makes n-gram overlap with the source (and hence with any eval set the source contaminates) even weaker -- worse for detection, not better.

Internal overlap: the four formats are 4 views of one 339M-document set -- see all_config_verdict. Cross-format near-duplication is structural, not incidental, and the fix is a hash partition of the id space.
needs_streaming_count_note: EMPTY -- all four of Phase 0's entries are resolved. faq, math, table and tutorial are all measured at high confidence from parquet footers, with no datasets-server dependency and no Batch job. The `all` config needs no count: it is a declared superset of the other four and must not be drawn from. The random-offset short-rewrite re-sample Phase 0 asked for is done at n=160,000 across 160 files.
open_items: The rewrite is length-biased against long source documents (median per-doc ratio 0.31-0.71 vs pooled 0.24-0.44, because max_tokens=2048 truncates the tail). If the reservoir cares about long-document structure, the synthetic pool under-supplies it. Not a blocker; a known distortion to record in the dataset README.

Cross-format id-disjoint slicing and synthetic-vs-edu-web id exclusion both need the `id` column carried through ingestion. If the ingestion path drops `id`, both mitigations become impossible after the fact -- and per project memory, labels inside manifest_sha256 are unbackfillable. Decide before the first publish.

files_written.artifacts/recount/_fp_footer_leaf.py: Phase 0c measurement tool. Nested-LEAF footer reader: matches column chunks on path_in_schema == 'rollout_results.list.element.text' (never on md.schema.names.index('text'), which returns the ORIGINAL because 'text' appears twice in the flat leaf list). Scales sampled-file leaf bytes by the exact per-config parquet byte total from the Hub tree API; validates that scaling against the independently-known row counts. Calibrates the footer's nested-leaf rep/def-level overhead by comparing footer bytes against sum(len(text.encode('utf8'))) on the row groups it actually reads. Tokenizes rewrite AND original from the same rows for a paired ratio. Threaded footer scan; no datasets-server dependency.
files_written.artifacts/recount/_fp_cluster_var.py: Cluster-variance sampler for the short-rewrite distribution. Reads one random row group from each of N random files and reports the PER-ROW-GROUP statistic distribution, so the SE accounts for the fact that a row group is 1000 content-clustered consecutive rows. Exists because Phase 0's n=34 head sample was one such cluster and was wrong by 10x.
files_written.artifacts/recount/_fp_leaf_raw.json: raw per-config output of both tools (footer totals, calibration, percentiles, per-group summary stats), 30 KB.
files_written.artifacts/recount/recount_finephrase.py: Phase 0's datasets-server-based tool. SUPERSEDED for counting and its HTTP path remains unvalidated -- do not use it: /size, /rows and /info all return HTTP 500 for config faq, and the /rows quota is per-IP. Its `rewrite_of()` schema path and its card-anchored estimator logic are correct and were both independently confirmed by Phase 0c.
